item.title: Peoria County election delays early voting due to court case
item.description: Early voting and vote-by-mail in Peoria County have been delayed due to an appellate court decision involving a Republican candidate for governor, Joseph Severino, who is appealing a decision to remove his name from the ballot due to a lack of valid petition signatures.

item.title: Nearly $19 million in federal funding secured for projects across Central Illinois
item.description: Congressman Darin LaHood announced that nearly $19 million in federal funding is headed to communities across Central and Northwestern Illinois, including several projects in Peoria aimed at improving infrastructure and supporting economic growth.

item.title: ISU students connect with employers at career fair
item.description: Illinois State University held a career fair for students on Thursday afternoon, featuring nearly 100 different companies and advice on resume construction, job interviews, and free headshots.

item.title: Veterans find healing and connection through art therapy
item.description: Heartland Community College is displaying artwork from their "Creativets" class, which teaches veterans the power of art, and is dedicated to a student who was killed in a car accident.

item.title: Winding road to the new $160M Par-A-Dice Casino barge proposal
item.description: Boyd Gaming's proposed $160 million redevelopment of the Par-A-Dice Casino Hotel was met with a surprise change, keeping the casino on the river instead of the previously proposed artificial pond, and the Illinois Gaming Board has tabled the vote until a special meeting in three weeks.

item.title: Housing market in Twin Cities expected to stabilize in 2026
item.description: The housing market in the Twin Cities is expected to improve in 2026 due to lower interest rates, while inventory will remain low due to population growth and a lack of multi-family housing.

item.title: Peoria Heights board of trustees delay grocery tax vote until after election day
item.description: Peoria Heights residents will vote on March 17th to decide whether to keep the 1% grocery tax, with the board of trustees set to discuss the issue on March 18th, and the mayor confident that the tax will be repealed.

item.title: Illinois Gaming Board delays vote on Par-A-Dice after stunning change
item.description: The Illinois Gaming Board has approved Boyd Gaming's Par-A-Dice Casino redevelopment plan in Easter Peoria, but the plan is still pending the result of a court hearing next week, with the city of Peoria arguing that the proposal is not enough to satisfy a 1991 agreement between Peoria and East Peoria.

item.title: New fully electric semi-truck on display at Annual Midwest Truck and Trailer Show
item.description: Tesla's new fully electric, heavy duty semi-truck will be on display at the 2026 Midwest Truck and Trailer Show in Peoria, Illinois, alongside hundreds of other commercial vehicles, parts exhibitors, and industry technology demonstrations, to answer questions and allow attendees to experience the newly designed Semi up close.

item.title: Honoring Black History: 100 years of celebrating Black history
item.description: Black History Month was founded in 1926 by Dr. Carter G. Woodson to celebrate the contributions of Black people to American society, and has since evolved into a national celebration of Black history.
